summary: Bhatt proves the direct summand conjecture, that a finite extension of a Noetherian regular ring splits as a module map (Theorem 1.1), and its derived variant: for proper surjective X0→Spec(A0) with A0 regular, A0→RΓ(X0,O) splits in D(A0) (Theorem 1.2). The proof reproves André's flatness lemma geometrically (Theorem 2.3), proves a quantitative Riemann extension theorem for perfectoid rings (Theorem 4.2) using almost mathematics of pro-systems (§3), and builds faithfully flat perfectoid covers of regular local rings (Proposition 5.2). After review and the confirmed red-team fixes the extraction has 90 items (66 missing, 14 planned, 10 library) in nine routes. The covers, obstruction calculus and both splitting theorems coalesce with the new roadmap DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay, and the Riemann extension theorem with the Part II of Perfectoid rings and spaces. The rest are sources for existing layers: PerfectoidSpaces P0–P3, PerfectoidQuotients Q3, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1/E2/E5, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4 and AdicSpacesPartII R2. The atlas lacks non-Noetherian flattening, the Cohen structure theorem, pro-systems of modules and almost mathematics of pro-systems. Twenty-five source findings: E1 (Proposition 6.2 needs surjectivity) affects a stated result; E9, E14 and E15 are gaps in the reductions of Theorems 5.4 and 6.1; E4–E8 are misprints in André's adjacent paper; the rest are misprints. G1 (collation with the published text) stays open.

items.name: Artin–Rees
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, submodule N and ideal I, there is k such that for all n≥k, I^n M∩N=I^(n−k)(I^k M∩N).
proofSteps: Read the actual statement with its finite-module and Noetherian hypotheses.

items.name: Uniform Artin–Rees lifting
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, ideal I and N⊂M, there is k independent of P and the surjection φ:P→N such that every v∈N∩I^(m+k)M lifts through φ to I^m P for every m.
proofSteps: The library quantifies k before P, φ and m. This is an available stronger control lemma, not a claim that 5.3 itself is already formalized.

items.name: Krull intersection for a proper ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, finite R-module M and proper ideal I, the intersection of I^n M is zero; in particular the intersection of I^n in R is zero.
proofSteps: Use this to detect a nonzero obstruction before adjoining roots, and to force a proper ideal containing all roots of p to be impossible.

items.name: Almost modules and adjoints
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) with m²=m and tilde m=m⊗_V m flat, form the Serre quotient by m-annihilated modules and almostification M↦M^a. For an almost module A, its right adjoint is A_*=Hom_{V^a}(V^a,A), with (N^a)_*≅Hom_V(tilde m,N) naturally. Its module left adjoint is A_!=tilde m⊗_V A_*. The algebra left adjoint (!!) is distinct. The simpler Hom_V(m,N) formula requires that multiplication tilde m→m be an isomorphism, in particular when m is flat.

items.note: Import PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base and P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints: the latter already states the tensor-square formula over a general basic setup. Do not restrict the general base by assuming m flat. Bhatt footnote 5 uses the flat perfectoid valuation ideal and is valid in that scope; the earlier general Hom_V(m,N) API was an extraction error, not a source erratum. The algebra adjoint (!!) used in Proposition 5.2 remains the separate algebra-adjoint item, routed to P0.
proofSteps: Use the general Hom formula and module adjunctions from P0, not a valuation-only formula. Base extension preserves flatness of the tensor square even when it does not preserve flatness of the image ideal.
Keep the module (!) and algebra (!!) adjoints distinct in faithful detection.

items.name: Bhatt's field-based integral perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field and fix t∈K° with 0<|t|<1 (a pseudouniformizer, i.e. a topologically nilpotent unit of K) admitting compatible p-power roots t^(1/p^k), with |t|=|p| when K has characteristic 0. An integral perfectoid K°-algebra is a K°-flat, t-adically complete K°-algebra A with A=A_* (if f∈A[1/t] and t^(1/p^k)f∈A for all k≥0 then f∈A) such that Frobenius induces an isomorphism A/t^(1/p)≃A/t.

proofSteps: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness of each neighborhood
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and each l>0, A/t→B_l/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.

Use the completed root-relation presentation of rational-model, needed only modulo t^ε with ε<1 (Scholze's proof of Lemma 6.4 gives it modulo ϖ).
At root level k reduce modulo t^ε for ε=1/p^(k+1); Frobenius identifies the quotient with a free, faithful polynomial-root algebra modulo T−g.

Pass through the filtered colimit over k and the ordinary t-adic completion (reduction modulo t^ε of a t-adic completion equals that of the module). Then go from t^ε to t using that A and B_ℓ are t-torsion-free. No derived presentation or derived completion is used (Remark 2.5); the almost category remains m_t.

items.name: Perfection of a simplicial F_p-algebra is discrete
items.statement: For a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra C, its filtered colimit along Frobenius is discrete and identifies with the perfection of π_0(C).

items.name: Root annihilation of torsion in a perfect ring
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra with compatible roots of t and tx=0, then t^(1/p^n)x=0 for every n.
proofSteps: Taking inverse Frobenius gives t^(1/p^n)x^(1/p^n)=0; multiply by x^(1−1/p^n), represented by a nonnegative power of x^(1/p^n).

items.name: Almost discreteness of the derived root presentation
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and f_1,…,f_n,g in its integral tilt, let B be the filtered colimit over r of the Koszul complexes over A[T_i^(1/p∞)] on the relations (g^(1/p^r))♯ T_i^(1/p^r)−(f_i^(1/p^r))♯. Then Kos(B;t) is almost discrete. For an admissible rational presentation, derived t-completion of B is almost its integral rational localization.
items.note: Remark 2.5 asks whether the presentations of [Sc1, Lemma 6.4] used in §2 also hold with the relations imposed in the derived sense, and answers yes by this lemma. §2 does not need it, but such presentations are used later, for instance the mod-t^m presentation of A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m in the proof of Theorem 4.2. The review folded the former item derived-presentation (Remark 2.5) into this one. The second assertion needs an admissible rational presentation, which the paper leaves implicit (E12).
proofSteps: Reduce to the characteristic-p tilt, perfect the derived polynomial relation algebra, then use root annihilation of its t-torsion.

Recover the completed comparison from reduction modulo t via DD.1. Split the discreteness and completion clauses in the final blueprint. items.name: Functorial almost faithful absolutely integrally closed extension
items.statement: For every integral perfectoid K°-algebra A there is a map A→B(A) of integral perfectoid K°-algebras, functorial in A, that is almost faithfully flat modulo t and such that B(A) is absolutely integrally closed (every monic polynomial over B(A) has a root); in particular every b∈B(A) has a compatible system of p-power roots.
items.note: Existing node PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma read. Its statement does not explicitly give the functorial choice required here.
proofSteps: Q3 already owns the stronger p-completely faithfully flat existence theorem for general perfectoid rings. Request only the functoriality and exact field-based comparison of this source, not a second AIC construction.

items.name: Almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: For a tower of A-modules M_n, almost-pro-zero means: for every k≥0 and n≥1 there exists m≥n such that t^(1/p^k) kills the image M_m→M_n. The later index may depend on both k and n.
proofSteps: This quantifier order is the input to all inverse-limit arguments.

items.name: Tower separating two almost notions
items.statement: Let A and t be as in Notation 3.1 with t not a unit (e.g. A=K°). Let M_n=A/(t^(1/p^n)), with transition M_(n+1)→M_n given by 1↦t^(1/p^n−1/p^(n+1)). These maps are injective and each M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) for m≥k, so {M_n} is almost-pro-zero; but the corresponding pro-object of the almost category is nonzero, since the image of M_m→M_n is generated by t^(1/p^n−1/p^m) and is not killed by t^(1/p^k) for k>m. If t is a unit, every M_n is zero.
proofSteps: For fixed k, M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) once m≥k. For any fixed transition into M_n, a sufficiently small positive root fails to kill its image in the valuation-ring example.

items.name: Derived inverse limit of an almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: If M_n is almost-pro-zero, every cohomology group of Rlim_n M_n is almost zero.
proofSteps: For each k the quotient tower M_n/M_n[t^(1/p^k)] is pro-zero. Apply pro-zero-roos and the short exact sequence to identify the two derived limits.
The two-term Roos complex of M_n[t^(1/p^k)] is termwise killed by t^(1/p^k). Thus each root annihilates the resulting cohomology.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphisms induce almost inverse-limit isomorphisms
items.statement: A morphism of coherent countable towers of A-module complexes whose cone cohomology towers are m_t-almost-pro-zero induces an almost isomorphism on derived inverse limits. This applies to the actual bounded-complex comparisons in 3.2–3.5; coherence is retained in D(Tower(Mod_A)) or an equivalent enhancement.
proofSteps: Use the functorial cone tower rather than choose unrelated cones in D(A). The exact Roos construction commutes with this cone.

Apply module-tower-milnor to the cone tower. For each a=t^(1/p^k), rlim-zero makes lim and lim-one of its almost-pro-zero cohomology towers killed by a, so both ends of each Milnor extension are almost zero.
Explicitly choose b=t^(1/p^(k+1)); b² kills the middle term, and t^(1/p^k)=b²·b^(p−2). This records the annihilator product that an extension requires.

items.name: A-linear functors preserve almost-pro-zero
items.statement: If F:Mod_A→Mod_A is A-linear and M_n is almost-pro-zero, then F(M_n) is almost-pro-zero.
proofSteps: Factor a sufficiently late transition through M_n[t^(1/p^k)]; A-linearity makes its image under F factor through F(M_n)[t^(1/p^k)]. No exactness assumption on F is needed.

items.name: Pointwise almost-zero kernels
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, for every m≥0 and n≥1, ker(A/t^m→A_n/t^m) is m_t-almost zero.
proofSteps: In the root-relation model, almost regularity of g modulo t^m controls the kernel; transport through the m_t-almost comparison.

items.name: Uniform root annihilation of cokernel transitions
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, working in m_t-almost modules, for every m,k≥0 the transition coker(f_(n+c))→coker(f_n) is annihilated by g^(1/p^k) for all n, where c=p^k m.
proofSteps: Represent monomials by u^e. For e≥p^(−k), the factor t^(ce) vanishes modulo t^m.
For e<p^(−k), multiply by g^(1/p^k) and rewrite it as a base element with exponents g^(p^(−k)−e)t^((n+c)e). The shift c is independent of n.

items.name: Quantitative Riemann extension
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, {A/t^m}_n→{A_n/t^m}_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism for the ideal generated by compatible roots of tg.
proofSteps: Combine the m_t kernel comparison and m_g cokernel estimate after explicit change of almost base.

items.name: Uniform derived tensor version
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1 and fixed m≥1, for every k≥0 set c=p^k m. For every K∈D(A/t^m), every i and every n≥1, g^(1/p^k) kills the c-step transition on the kernels and cokernels of H^i(K)→H^i(K⊗^L_(A/t^m) A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m) in m_t-almost modules. Consequently (tg)^(1/p^k) kills those ordinary transitions, with c independent of n, K and i. For m=0 both rings modulo t^0 are zero.
items.note: The prior G4 chain-level gap is resolved at the paper-proof level by the amplitude-zero cone argument. This is not a claim that the derived tensor API is implemented.
proofSteps: Theorem 4.2(1) identifies the almost cone of each comparison with its module cokernel, naturally in n.
Theorem 4.2(2) makes g^(1/p^k) times the c-step map of those cokernels exactly zero in almost modules, for c=p^k m.
Apply uniform-tensor-cone and tensor-kernel-cokernel. This proves the stated bound without a ghost-map assumption. The general almost derived tensor implementation remains supplied by E1/P0.

items.name: Uniform estimates for Koszul homology
items.statement: For a regular sequence in A/t^m in the setup of 4.2, nonzero-degree Koszul homology of its base change to A_n/t^m forms uniformly almost-pro-zero towers. The underlying comparison applies to any finite Koszul complex, but vanishing of the source homology uses regularity.
proofSteps: Import generic Koszul construction from DD.1; specialize its derived base-change map.

items.name: Riemann extension without regularity of g
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, the final almost-pro-isomorphism of 4.2 holds without the almost nonzerodivisor hypothesis on g modulo t^m.
proofSteps: Apply the regular universal case K°⟨T^(1/p∞)⟩ with T, derived base change T↦g, and take H^0. This does not assert the separate pointwise kernel statement for arbitrary g.

items.statement: Under the introductory setup, A∞→lim_n A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is almost an isomorphism with respect to roots of pg, using the reductions and limits over m of 1.6.
proofSteps: Recover completeness by the limit over m and account for derived inverse-limit terms; this is weaker information than the quantitative tower theorem.

items.name: Lifting flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: For A Noetherian and A→B, if π is a nonzerodivisor on both rings, both are π-adically complete and A/π→B/π is flat, then A→B is flat.
proofSteps: Resolve a finite A-module by finite free modules; compare tensor with Rlim of reductions.
Finite generation bounds π-power torsion, making the extra Tor tower pro-zero. Lift flatness to all π^n reductions, then use left t-exactness of Rlim.

items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as 5.1, faithful flatness of A/π→B/π implies faithful flatness of A→B.
proofSteps: Every maximal ideal of π-complete A contains π. Its residue field remains nonzero after tensor with B/π; use the existing faithful-flatness criterion.

items.name: Almost Tor vanishing for regular local covers
items.statement: For p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 with residue characteristic p, there exists field-based integral perfectoid A as in 5.2 with Tor_i^A0(M,A) m_p-almost zero for every A0-module M and i>0.
proofSteps: Unramified case: A0→A is faithfully flat (unramified-cover), so the positive Tor groups vanish.

Ramified case (p. 9): factor A0→A′→A_!!→A, with (−)_!! as in [GR, Definition 2.2.23] (algebra-adjoint). A0→A′ is faithfully flat; (−)_!! commutes with reduction modulo p^m [GR, Remark 2.2.28(ii)], so the almost faithful flatness of A′→A modulo p^m and [GR, Remark 3.1.3(ii)] make A′→A_!! faithfully flat modulo p^m. A_!! is p-adically complete and p-torsionfree, so Proposition 5.1 makes A0→A_!! faithfully flat. A_!!→A is an injective almost isomorphism, so Tor_i^{A0}(M,A) is almost zero for i>0; retain quantification over all M.

The source proves A′→A almost faithfully flat only modulo π, and A′ is not Noetherian. Do not replace the A_!! route by composing with an integrally almost flat A′→A unless an almost version of Proposition 5.1 is proved first.

Reduce a nonzero M to a cyclic submodule and use almost flatness; containing every root of p would put p in all powers of a proper ideal, contrary to Krull intersection.
This ordinary detection conclusion is distinct from faithfulness in the almost category.

items.name: Reduction to complete mixed-characteristic regular local rings
items.statement: To prove the finite splitting theorem, use localization, faithfully flat completion and residue-field extension to reduce the mixed-characteristic branch to a complete regular local ring A0 of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field, and a finite injective domain extension A0→B0 that is finite étale after inverting pg for some g∈A0 coprime to p. Here g lies outside every minimal prime of pA0, so g≠0 in A0/p, as the Krull step of 5.4 requires. Complete before passing to a domain quotient of B0, since completion need not preserve the domain property.
items.note: Continuation 4 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 2026-09-29): the finite-domain part of this reduction is not in the paper (E9); it is proved here as a named step.
proofSteps: Prove descent of existence of a retraction via the finite obstruction module, the component/domain reductions and existence of a discriminant element. These are named unfinished inputs G5, not automatic changes of hypotheses.

items.name: Detecting a surviving finite splitting obstruction
items.statement: In the complete local finite-extension setup of 5.4, a nonzero splitting obstruction remains nonzero modulo p^m for some m≥3, and after the two almost faithful extensions there is k such that (pg)^(1/p^k) does not annihilate the resulting obstruction.
proofSteps: Use finite Hom and vanishing lim¹ to detect nonzero reduction; choose k with p²g outside the relevant annihilator power; account for the loss of one factor p in almost-flat base change.
The p²g→pg calculation must be expanded at declaration level; retain it as G5 rather than suppressing its bound.

items.name: Almost purity for finite étale perfectoid extensions
items.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring R and a finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S° is almost finite étale over R° (ECD Theorem 6.1); when R is a perfectoid K-algebra, S° is moreover uniformly almost finitely generated over R° ([Sc1, Theorem 7.9(iii)]). The ramified case of 5.2 applies this over the generalized perfectoid ring A′[1/p], which need not contain a perfectoid field, so it needs the Tate-ring form (the paper points to [SW, §6], [GR2, §16], [KL, §3]); 5.4 and 6.2 need only the field case. Faithfulness is a separate hypothesis when a cover or almost retraction is needed.
proofSteps: Import the accepted partial node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem for the field case, preserving its proof gaps, and P3's stage-level ECD Theorem 6.1 for perfectoid Tate rings. That node records that the Tate-ring proof ([KL15, 3.6.21, 5.5.9], [Fal02]) was not read, so the generalized form remains an open supplier obligation of P3.

items.name: Almost splitting of a finite generically étale cover
items.statement: For the finite injective extensions over the rational perfectoid algebras in 5.4, finite étale after inverting p, the unit is almost split with respect to m_p.

items.name: Annihilation of the finite obstruction on each annulus
items.statement: For fixed m,n in the setup of 5.4, the obstruction after base change to A∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m is m_p-almost zero.
proofSteps: The rational inequality makes g invertible after p is inverted, so the chosen generic étaleness applies.

items.name: Recovering almost vanishing over A∞
items.statement: In the setup of 5.4, annular almost vanishing implies that the obstruction over A∞/p^m is m_(pg)-almost zero.
proofSteps: Theorem 4.2 is applied with A=A∞, t=p and g, but the proof never checks its Notation 4.1 hypothesis (g an almost nonzerodivisor modulo p^m). Discharge it by Remark 4.4 (remove-regularity), or directly: g coprime to p is a nonzerodivisor on the Cohen–Macaulay ring A0/p^m, and A0/p^m→A∞/p^m is almost flat.
Apply the A∞-linear Hom functor to the tower; it becomes almost-pro-isomorphic to a constant system. Lemma 3.5 removes the lim¹ obstruction, contradicting detection.

Since Hom_{A∞}(Q∞,−) is not exact, apply Lemma 3.6 to the A∞-linear functors Hom_{D(A∞)}(Q∞,−[j]) on the kernel and cokernel towers of Theorem 4.2's map, and combine them with the long exact sequences. All almost statements here are with respect to (pg)^{1/p^∞}.

items.name: Direct summand theorem
items.statement: For a finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular, there exists an A0-linear map B0→A0 whose composite with the unit is the identity.
items.note: Continuation 4 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 2026-09-29): statement as in Theorem 1.1; Theorem 5.4 as printed omits the extension (E10). The same theorem is an item of PAPER-ANDRE-18-B with André's proof; the coalesced route keeps one theorem with two proofs. Remark 5.5 (p. 10) observes that the proof of Theorem 5.4 goes through for any Noetherian ring admitting a faithfully flat integral perfectoid extension, and asks whether that condition characterises regularity; G8 records the later answer. The review folded the former item perfectoid-kunz into this note, since the remark is not a step towards the main results.
proofSteps: Combine the mixed-characteristic contradiction with the separately supplied equal-characteristic cases and descent. The retraction is module-linear, not a ring homomorphism.

items.name: Perfect proper coherent cohomology over a regular local base
items.statement: For proper X→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian, RΓ(X,O_X) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology modules, so it is pseudo-coherent; when A0 is a regular local ring it is a perfect complex of A0-modules.
items.locator: Theorem 6.1 proof, p. 11. It is implicit in 'We may assume A0 is a regular local ring', since localizing the splitting obstruction needs a pseudo-coherent cone. It is also implicit in 'Repeating the argument in the proof of Theorem 5.4', since the flat base change of its Hom along A0→A∞ needs a perfect cone.
items.note: Every input is planned, but no layer plans this corollary, so it stays missing and is routed with the splitting theorems (review). Tau Ceti StableReduction layer 2 plans coherent pushforward and R^i f_* under proper morphisms over locally Noetherian bases. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans "a Noetherian local ring is regular iff it has finite global dimension", and P7 (node perfect-complexes-tor-amplitude-and-minimal-models) plans "a bounded complex with perfect cohomology is perfect". Boundedness comes from a finite affine Čech cover of the separated, quasi-compact X. The unit-compatible comparison with cohomology of an ordinary base change is the separate item cohomology-base-change-map, and 6.1 needs no isomorphism there. The owner imports these layers rather than re-planning proper coherent finiteness, which is a Tau Ceti layer.
proofSteps: Import coherent pushforward R^i f_* for proper morphisms over locally Noetherian bases (StableReduction layer 2): each H^i(X,O_X) is a finite A0-module.
X is separated and quasi-compact, so a finite affine Čech cover computes RΓ(X,O_X) and bounds its amplitude.

Over a Noetherian A0 a bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology is pseudo-coherent. A regular local A0 has finite global dimension (R03.3), so each finite H^i is perfect, and a bounded complex with perfect cohomology is perfect (P7).
The obstruction calculus of 6.1 uses the perfect cone of A0→RΓ(X,O_X): its Hom into A0[1] commutes with flat base change (Stacks 0A6A).

items.name: Generic multisection reduction
items.statement: Let A0 be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with fraction field K, and f0:X0→Spec(A0) proper and surjective. The generic fibre X0_K is a nonempty K-scheme of finite type, so it has a closed point x with κ(x) finite and separable over K. The reduced closure Z of x in X0 is integral, and proper, surjective and generically finite over Spec(A0). There is g∈A0 coprime to p such that Z→Spec(A0) is finite étale after inverting pg: no prime factor of p in the factorial ring A0 divides g, so g is a nonzerodivisor modulo p. The unit of Z factors as A0→RΓ(X0,O)→RΓ(Z,O), so a left inverse for Z gives one for X0.
proofSteps: Closed points of the nonempty finite-type K-scheme X0_K have residue fields finite over K, separable because K has characteristic 0.
The reduced closure Z is closed in X0, hence proper over A0. It is dominant, hence surjective, and its generic fibre is Spec κ(x).

The non-quasi-finite and non-étale loci of the proper map Z→Spec(A0) have closed images that miss the generic point. Pick h≠0 vanishing on both, and factor h in A0. The prime factors of h that divide p divide a power of p; let g be the product of the others. Then D(pg)⊂D(h). Over D(h) the map is proper, quasi-finite and étale, hence finite étale.
Following the unit of X0 by restriction RΓ(X0,O)→RΓ(Z,O) gives the unit of Z. Composing a left inverse for Z with this restriction gives one for X0.

items.name: Integral global functions in the perfectoid proper case
items.statement: For proper surjective Y→Spec(A) in the corrected 6.2 setup, B=H^0(Y,O_Y) is an integral A-algebra; B[1/p] is the finite étale generic algebra, and Y maps naturally to Spec(B).
items.note: Reclassified from missing after reading declarations at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Proper.lean:138 proves integrality for every universally closed morphism with affine target; no Noetherian or surjectivity hypothesis. QuasiSeparated.lean:401 identifies sections on a global basic open with localization for qcqs opens. GammaSpecAdjunction.lean:434,458 supplies the natural affinization map. The given proper morphism is qcqs, and Y[1/p] is its basic open for the image of p. Thus B[1/p]=Γ(Y[1/p],O), finite étale by the stated hypothesis. This is a composition of existing results, not a new general theorem to re-plan. No finiteness of B over A is asserted.
proofSteps: Apply isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed to Y→Spec(A).
Apply isLocalization_basicOpen_of_qcqs to the whole qcqs scheme Y and the image of p; identify the generic fibre with that basic open.
Use Scheme.toSpecΓ and its naturality for Y→Spec(A) to obtain Y→Spec(B) over Spec(A).

items.name: Admissible blowup domination of a generic isomorphism
items.statement: Let A be p-torsionfree and p-adically complete, and X→Spec(A) proper and an isomorphism after inverting p. There is a finitely generated ideal I⊂A containing p^N for some N≥1 and a factorization Bl_I(Spec(A))→X→Spec(A). This algebraic factorization is what 6.2 uses, since generic-fiber-map maps (Sη,O^+) into Bl_I(Spec(A)); completing it p-adically gives the formal domination the paper states.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2; exact algebraic supplier Stacks 081T, rather than a domination theorem attributed to GR2 §15.4
items.note: The proof source for domination has been identified. Foundational flattening leaves are still G6; GR2 §15.4 is used for rational charts and integral stalks, not mis-cited as a standalone domination theorem. Review: moved from AdicSpacesPartII R2 to SF.4, beside proper-modification-domination; R2 cannot import SF.4, which is its descendant.
proofSteps: Apply proper-modification-domination with U=D(p), a quasi-compact open of the affine qcqs base. Choose a finite list of generators for its centre and append p^N.
Each blowup chart A[I/f] is a subring of A[1/f]; p remains regular. Its p-adic completion is the chart for the completed admissible blowup.
Use the functorial completion of the algebraic diagram only if a formal version is desired. No Noetherian formal-functions or formal-GAGA theorem is invoked.

items.name: Integral generic-fiber factorization
items.statement: Let A be a p-adically complete, p-torsionfree ring such that the Huber pair (A[1/p],A) is sheafy, and let Sη=Spa(A[1/p],A). For every finitely generated ideal I=(f_0,…,f_r) of A containing p^N for some N≥1, the integral locally ringed space (Sη,O^+) maps over Spec(A) to Bl_I(Spec(A)), compatibly with the structure maps to Spec(A). A normalized integral perfectoid K°-algebra over a mixed-characteristic perfectoid field K is an example, sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces P2.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2 footnote 8; GR2 Release 6.95, Lemma 15.4.14(i)–(ii) and Remark 15.4.25(i)–(vi), pp. 1318–1324
items.note: Review: restated for sheafy pairs, and the composition with formal-domination moved to perfectoid-proper-split. As extracted it needed SF.4 and the perfectoid layers P2 and P3, all of which are descendants of R2.
proofSteps: Set U_i={x: |f_j(x)|≤|f_i(x)| for all j}. Append p^N to the generator list. These rational subsets cover Sη: at a given valuation one generator has maximal value, and that value is nonzero because |p^N|>0.
The ratios f_j/f_i are bounded sections on U_i. The map A[1/f_i]→O(U_i) restricts to A[I/f_i]→O^+(U_i), using the actual blowup algebra, including its torsion relations.
The integral stalks are local: GR2 15.4.14(ii) identifies them as the inverse image of the residual valuation ring. The chart map therefore gives a locally ringed-space map into Spec(A[I/f_i]).
On U_i∩U_j the two ratios are reciprocal bounded units. Both chart maps restrict to the same localized ring map, so glue.

Sheafiness of (A[1/p],A) is a hypothesis: for the perfectoid instance it is imported by the consumer perfectoid-proper-split from P2, which R2 cannot import. GR2 15.4.34 is not applied without its analytically Noetherian hypothesis.

items.name: Almost derived splitting over a perfectoid base
items.statement: Let K be a mixed-characteristic perfectoid field, A an integral perfectoid K°-algebra, and f:Y→Spec(A) proper with f[1/p] finite étale and surjective. Then A→RΓ(Y,O_Y) has a left inverse in the almost derived category for m_p.
proofSteps: Use the pinned integrality/localization/affinization imports for B=Γ(Y,O). Almost purity yields B→C, generic isomorphism and an almost finite étale surjective cover A→C with an almost A-linear retraction.

The morphism Y→Spec(B) is proper: its graph into Y×_A Spec(B) is closed because Spec(B) is separated over Spec(A), and projection is a base change of the original proper map. Thus Y_C is proper over C and has identity generic fibre.

Apply formal-domination to Y_C→Spec(C), and generic-fiber-map to the perfectoid pair (C[1/p],C), which is sheafy by P2, to factor (Sη,O^+)→Bl_I(Spec(C))→Y_C→Spec(C). Functoriality of structure-sheaf cohomology identifies C→RΓ(Y_C,O)→RΓ(Sη,O^+) with the unit, which acyclicity makes an almost isomorphism, so C→RΓ(Y_C,O) is almost split.
Restrict scalars and compose RΓ(Y,O)→RΓ(Y_C,O)→C→A. Its composite with A→RΓ(Y,O) is the identity in the almost derived category.

items.name: Derived direct summand theorem
items.statement: For any Noetherian regular ring A0 and proper surjective morphism f0:X0→Spec(A0), the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) admits a left inverse in D(A0).
proofSteps: Reduce by derived-local-reduction to complete regular local rings, and treat those of equal characteristic by equal-characteristic.

In mixed characteristic use the generic multisection, then the perfect-cone obstruction calculus (perfect-cone-detection, perfect-cone-limit) for the cone of A0→RΓ(X0,O), which is perfect by proper-cohomology. On each annulus apply 6.2 (perfectoid-proper-split) and splitting-through-comparison.

items.name: Equal-characteristic splitting inputs
items.statement: For regular Noetherian Q-algebras, the finite direct-summand theorem follows from normalized trace and the derived statement from the characteristic-zero rational-singularity splitting result. For regular Noetherian F_p-algebras use the positive-characteristic direct/derived splinter results cited in the introduction.
items.note: Continuation 4 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 2026-09-29): read Bhatt, Derived splinters in positive characteristic, arXiv:1109.0354v1 (sha256 4fa366d3…): Theorem 0.3 (a noetherian F_p-scheme is a splinter iff a derived splinter), Example 1.3 (regular affine F_p-schemes are splinters, Hochster) and Example 1.2 (for varieties over C, derived splinter iff rational singularities, Kovács). The paper's citations [Bh1, Theorem 1.4 & Example 2.3] and [Bh1, Theorem 2.12] use the published numbering, one section later. Kovács's statement is for varieties over C, so the characteristic-0 branch for an arbitrary regular noetherian Q-algebra needs the reduction recorded in the route brief (completion, Popescu approximation). Review (REV-PAPER-BHATT-18, 2026-09-29): v1 also has Theorem 0.4, on finite covers annihilating higher cohomology, from which Theorem 0.3 follows. A one-section shift therefore matches [Bh1, Theorem 1.4] to v1 Theorem 0.4 and [Bh1, Example 2.3] to v1 Example 1.3. No v1 statement is numbered 1.12: §1 ends at Example 1.11, and the Kovács statement is Example 1.2. So [Bh1, Theorem 2.12] is unverified against v1 and needs the published Compositio text (G1).
proofSteps: Read exact hypotheses and reduction from the original cited cases before treating these branches as closed; G7. Characteristic zero here must mean a Q-algebra/equal-characteristic reduction, not merely char(A)=0.

items.name: Cone of an almost injective module map
items.statement: For a commutative almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the standard flatness hypothesis on m⊗V m, a V-algebra R, and an R-module map u:M→N whose kernel is almost zero, Cone(u)^a is naturally isomorphic to coker(u)^a placed in degree zero. The isomorphism is natural in commutative squares of module maps.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, expanded from Theorem 4.2(1); ordinary cochain convention H^(-1)(Cone(u))=ker(u)
proofSteps: The two-term cone has cohomology only in degrees −1 and 0. Exact almostification removes its degree −1 cohomology.
The canonical projection Cone(u)→coker(u)[0] is therefore a quasi-isomorphism after almostification; its naturality identifies the actual transition maps, not only the objects.

items.name: Uniform tensor annihilation from module cokernels
items.statement: Let u_n:M→N_n be a compatible countable tower of module maps over R, each almost injective for m. Put Q_n=coker(u_n). If a·(Q_(n+c)→Q_n)=0 in almost R-modules for all n, then for every K∈D(R), a annihilates the transition Cone(K⊗^L u_(n+c))→Cone(K⊗^L u_n) in the almost derived category. The same c works for every K and every cohomological degree.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3; explicit derivation of its same-constant assertion
proofSteps: Use the natural cone-to-cokernel equivalence before applying derived tensor. The transition multiplied by a is the zero morphism of modules, hence zero in the derived category.
Derived tensor is R-linear and exact. Almostification commutes with derived tensor under the fixed almost-base hypotheses, so K^a⊗^L Q_n^a computes the almostified tensor cone.
Neither boundedness nor flatness of K is assumed: use the K-flat derived tensor supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1. Do not replace equality of morphisms by mere vanishing of their cohomology maps.

items.name: Uniform annihilation of tensor comparison defects
items.statement: Under uniform-tensor-cone, a kills the transition maps on both ker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) and coker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) in almost modules, for all i, with the same shift c. For m=m_t and a=g^(1/p^k), every t^(1/p^j)g^(1/p^k) kills the corresponding ordinary transition maps. In particular (tg)^(1/p^k) works with j=k.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, long exact cohomology sequence of the tensor cone
proofSteps: In each degree, the cokernel of H^i(u) embeds in H^i(Cone(u)), while the kernel of H^i(u) is a quotient of H^(i−1)(Cone(u)). These are natural descriptions for the transition squares.
Restrict or pass to the quotient of the zero scalar transition; no extra shift or squaring of g is needed.
A morphism which is zero after almostification has m-annihilated image. Multiply by each specified root of t to return to ordinary modules.

items.statement: For a countable pro-zero tower M_n of R-modules, 1−s on ∏M_n is invertible. Hence lim M_n=lim¹ M_n=0 and Rlim M_n=0. More generally, a levelwise morphism of module towers whose kernel and cokernel towers are pro-zero induces an isomorphism on derived inverse limits.

Its local presentation lemma 38.3.2 reduces via a finite pushforward to a smooth affine morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres.

Lemma 38.30.3 gives a finite locally free locus surjecting over the base. A chosen free submodule is universally injective by 38.10.1; its cokernel has smaller fibre-support dimension, so apply induction.
After making U schematically dense, 38.11.1 supplies finite presentation. These invoked proof leaves and the étale gluing in 38.30.6 remain explicit source-closure obligations, not assumed solved.
items.note: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 also plans 'flattening by blowup, strict transforms' as finite-type scheme geometry for de Jong's alterations over excellent Noetherian bases. The theorem here (Stacks 0815: qcqs base, no Noetherian hypothesis) covers that use. One owner should export it and L5 should import it, so that the atlas does not plan flattening twice. The auxiliary Stacks leaves (38.3.2, 38.30.3, 38.30.6, 38.10.1, 38.11.1 and Divisors 31.34.7) remain source-closure obligations in G6.

items.name: Flattening a finite type scheme generically of finite presentation
items.statement: For qcqs S, quasi-compact open U, and a finite type quasi-separated X→S whose restriction to U is flat and locally of finite presentation, some U-admissible blowup makes the strict transform X′ flat and finitely presented over S′.
proofSteps: Cover X by finitely many affines and find a common admissible refinement of the blowups for them (Stacks 080N, Lemma 31.35.4, with Remark 38.30.1).
Embed each affine as a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open V in affine space over S. Apply flattening-modification to i_*O_X on V.

Strict transform commutes with affine pushforward (Stacks 080G, Lemma 31.34.4, still a supplier obligation). Finite presentation of the transformed structure sheaf then gives finite presentation of the scheme.

items.name: A flat generic isomorphism is an open immersion
items.statement: If f:X→S is separated, locally of finite type and flat, and U⊂S is retrocompact and schematically dense with f^(-1)(U)→U an isomorphism, then f is an open immersion.
proofSteps: The source first proves local finite presentation and zero-dimensional fibres via 38.11.2–38.11.3, then reduces around a point to a finite component in an elementary étale neighbourhood (37.41.6).
Flatness transports schematic density of U; the extraneous component is empty. The resulting finite locally free morphism has rank one on the dense open, hence everywhere after localization.
These local finite-presentation, fibre-dimension and étale-neighbourhood inputs remain individually named in G6. The generic-isomorphism hypothesis alone is not enough without flatness.

items.name: A proper generic isomorphism is dominated by a blowup
items.statement: Let S be qcqs and U⊂S quasi-compact open. Every proper X→S which is an isomorphism over U admits a factorization S′→X→S with S′→S a U-admissible blowup. Neither S nor X is required Noetherian.
proofSteps: First blow up an ideal of finite type defining the complement of U in S so that its inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor; then U is schematically dense.
Flatten the strict transform; flat-generic-isomorphism makes it an open subscheme of S′.
The strict transform is also proper over S′, so this open immersion is closed. Its image contains dense U; it is all of S′.
Compose the admissible blowups using 31.35.2. For S=Spec(A), U=D(p), finite generation and I[1/p]=A[1/p] imply p^N∈I for some N.

items.name: Unit-compatible derived cohomology base-change map
items.statement: For any ring map R→D and a qcqs R-scheme X, put X_D=X×_R Spec(D). There is a natural D-linear map β:RΓ(X,O_X)⊗^L_R D→RΓ(X_D,O_(X_D)), compatible with the units from D. No flatness or Tor-independence is required to construct β; neither isomorphism nor almost isomorphism is asserted.
items.locator: Stacks 08HY, Remark 20.28.3; Bhatt Theorem 6.1 final diagram chase
proofSteps: For the cartesian square, construct Lg* Rf*→Rf′* Lg′* by the adjunction counit, as in 08HY. Apply it to O_X; Lg′*O_X=O_(X_D).
Identify quasi-coherent derived modules on the affine bases with ring-module complexes, importing this comparison from the existing sheaf foundations.
The triangle identities give β∘unit_derived=unit_ordinary. This is the sole base-change relation needed in the splitting argument.

uses.where: Stacks 08HY, Remark 20.28.3; Bhatt Theorem 6.1 final diagram chase

unitTests.statement: For X=Spec(B), β is the canonical B⊗^L_R D→B⊗_R D.

items.name: Transfer a retraction across a compatible comparison
items.statement: In any category, if u:A→M, v:M→N, and r:N→A satisfy r∘v∘u=id_A, then v followed by r is a retraction of u. In D(D), an almost retraction of D→RΓ(X_D,O) therefore composes with cohomology-base-change-map to split D→RΓ(X,O)⊗^L_R D almost. A further derived scalar extension preserves a supplied retraction.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.1 final sentence and 6.2 change of base; elementary composition in a category
proofSteps: Compose the supplied maps and use the unit triangle. Associativity proves the retraction identity; no conservativity, faithful flat descent or inverse of β is used.

For 6.1 first work over D=A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ and then apply −⊗^L_D D/p^m. Since p is regular on D, this is the displayed reduction of its unit; the left-hand derived scalar extension is already the object in the proof.

For 6.2 use the algebra map B→C to get Y_C→Y and a map RΓ(Y,O)→RΓ(Y_C,O). Compose the retraction to C with the almost retraction C→A from almost purity. The base change is along B, so no unproved A-flatness of B→C is required.

items.name: Tilt of an integral perfectoid algebra and the sharp map
items.statement: For an integral perfectoid K°-algebra A, A♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} A/t is an integral perfectoid K♭°-algebra, with t♭ = (t, t^(1/p), t^(1/p²), …) ∈ A♭. The map ♯: A♭→A, (x_n)_n ↦ lim_n x̃_n^(p^n) for arbitrary lifts x̃_n ∈ A, is well defined and multiplicative with (t♭)♯ = t, and projection to the first coordinate gives a ring isomorphism A♭/t♭ ≅ A/t.
items.locator: Lemma 2.6 and its proof (p. 5: f_i, g ∈ A♭ and their sharps); proof of Theorem 2.3 (p. 4: f ∈ A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩♭ and f♯)
items.note: Added in review. P1 plans the multiplicative inverse limit defining R♭, its addition and topology, the sharp map and the descriptions of the integral subrings, which give A♭ as the integral subring of (A[1/t])♭ (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, §5).
proofSteps: Import P1's tilt, sharp map and integral-subring description for the perfectoid K-algebra A[1/t], and identify A♭ with the integral subring of its tilt.

unitTests.statement: For K the completion of Q_p(p^(1/p^∞)), A = K° and t = p, A♭ is the t♭-adic completion of F_p[(t♭)^(1/p^∞)] and (t♭)♯ = p.

uses.where: Lemma 2.6 and its proof (p. 5: f_i, g ∈ A♭ and their sharps); proof of Theorem 2.3 (p. 4: f ∈ A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩♭ and f♯)
uses.how: Import P1's tilt, sharp map and integral-subring description for the perfectoid K-algebra A[1/t], and identify A♭ with the integral subring of its tilt.

items.name: Pro-zero towers and pro-isomorphisms of towers of modules
items.statement: An ℕ-indexed tower {M_n} of A-modules is pro-zero if for every n there is m ≥ n such that the transition map M_m→M_n is zero. A level map of towers {M_n}→{N_n} is a pro-isomorphism if its kernel and cokernel towers are pro-zero; equivalently, it is an isomorphism of pro-objects. Neither notion changes under passage to a cofinal subtower.
items.locator: Definition 3.2 (p. 6: 'a pro-isomorphism in the usual sense'); Lemma 5.3 (p. 9); proof of Lemma 3.4
items.note: Added in review. No layer plans pro-objects of modules, and Mathlib at 082e2d37 has Ind-objects but no pro-categories of modules. It is placed beside pro-zero-roos in E2, an ancestor of P0; hom-pro in R03.1 uses it too (see route 5).
proofSteps: Define both notions for ℕ-indexed towers and level maps, which is all the paper uses, and prove invariance under cofinal reindexing. The comparison with isomorphisms in the pro-category is optional.

unitTests.name: pro-tower.test_1
unitTests.statement: The tower {Z/p^n} with transition maps Z/p^(n+1)→Z/p^n, 1 ↦ p, is pro-zero: the composite from level 2n to level n is multiplication by p^n, which is zero on Z/p^n.

unitTests.name: pro-tower.test_2
unitTests.statement: The tower {Z/p^n} with the projections is not pro-zero, since every transition map is surjective onto a nonzero module.

uses.where: Definition 3.2 (p. 6: 'a pro-isomorphism in the usual sense'); Lemma 5.3 (p. 9); proof of Lemma 3.4
uses.how: Define both notions for ℕ-indexed towers and level maps, which is all the paper uses, and prove invariance under cofinal reindexing. The comparison with isomorphisms in the pro-category is optional.

items.name: Faithful flatness through the algebra adjoint (−)_!!
items.statement: In the ramified case of Proposition 5.2, let A′→A be the map to the completed integral closure, with almost mathematics measured by (p^(1/p^∞)) = (π^(1/p^∞)), and let A_!! be the A′-algebra attached to A by [GR, Definition 2.2.23]. Then A_!!→A is an injective almost isomorphism, A_!! is p-adically complete and p-torsionfree, the formation of (−)_!! commutes with reduction modulo p^m [GR, Remark 2.2.28(ii)], and if A′→A is almost faithfully flat modulo p^m, then A′→A_!! is faithfully flat modulo p^m [GR, Remark 3.1.3(ii)].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.2, ramified case, p. 9 ('This map factorizes as A0 → A′ → A_!! → A'); [GR, Definition 2.2.23, Remarks 2.2.28(ii) and 3.1.3(ii)]
items.note: Added in review. almost-category names the (!!) adjoint, but no item stated the properties 5.2(2) uses, and P0 plans the module adjoints but neither (−)_!! for algebras nor GR Remark 3.1.3(ii). The GR statements were not read in this review (G3).
proofSteps: The cokernel of A_!!→A is almost zero, hence killed by p = (p^(1/p))^p, so pA ⊂ A_!! ⊂ A. Then A_!! is p-torsionfree, open and hence closed in the p-adically complete A, and p-adically complete.
Import GR Remark 2.2.28(ii) for compatibility with reduction modulo p^m and GR Remark 3.1.3(ii) to pass from almost faithful flatness of A′/p^m→A/p^m to faithful flatness of A′/p^m→A_!!/p^m.

unitTests.name: algebra-adjoint.test_1
unitTests.statement: For every such A, pA ⊆ A_!! ⊆ A.

uses.where: Proof of Proposition 5.2, ramified case, p. 9 ('This map factorizes as A0 → A′ → A_!! → A'); [GR, Definition 2.2.23, Remarks 2.2.28(ii) and 3.1.3(ii)]
uses.how: The cokernel of A_!!→A is almost zero, hence killed by p = (p^(1/p))^p, so pA ⊂ A_!! ⊂ A. Then A_!! is p-torsionfree, open and hence closed in the p-adically complete A, and p-adically complete.

items.name: Cohen coefficient map for a perfect residue field
items.statement: Let (B,m,k) be a complete Noetherian local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k. Choose a continuous local coefficient map iota:W(k)→B inducing the identity on k. Its choice is part of the input to later presentations, and is retained in coefficient-change diagrams.
items.locator: Bhatt, proof of Proposition 5.2, p.8 (the common W=W(k) coefficient input); André, La conjecture du facteur direct, published §4.2 p.86 and §4.4(1) pp.87–88
items.note: Common input shared with accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/cohen-parameter-presentation and coefficient-ring-compatibility, route 4. Route once to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1, which owns coefficient categories and coefficient changes. The exact Cohen construction is a requested source addition, not a built declaration or a promised node treated as live. No new library search is asserted by this fix. The separable coefficient-change theorem remains the companion extraction’s cited input; its Matsumura proof was not reread here.
proofSteps: Request the common Cohen coefficient map and its residue-field compatibility from R03.1, coordinating the accepted André route; later consumers use that chosen map instead of reconstructing it.

api.statement: The composite W(k)→B→k is the canonical residue map, so the induced map on residue fields is the identity.

api.statement: Use the chosen coefficient map iota in the continuous homomorphism W(k)[[X_1,…,X_r]]→B taking each variable to a selected element of m.

api.statement: For a local map beta:B→B′ between complete Noetherian mixed-characteristic rings with perfect residue fields and separable k→k′, import the compatible coefficient-ring choices of PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/coefficient-ring-compatibility. Keep the commuting square beta∘iota=iota′∘W(k→k′) explicit; do not silently choose unrelated coefficient maps.

items.name: Regular-local presentations over an imported Cohen coefficient map
items.statement: Let (A0,m,k) be a complete Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) and dimension d, with k perfect. Import a chosen continuous local coefficient map iota:W(k)→A0 inducing the identity on k from cohen-coefficient-ring (R03.1). All presentations below are maps of W(k)-algebras for this chosen iota. If p ∉ m², then A0 ≅ W(k)⟦x_2,…,x_d⟧. If p ∈ m², any generators x_1,…,x_d of m give a surjection W(k)⟦x_1,…,x_d⟧→A0 whose kernel is generated by an element p−f with f a power series in (p,x_1,…,x_d)²; moreover p ∤ f and f has no constant term.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.2, pp. 8–9 ('A0 is isomorphic to W⟦x_2, ..., x_d⟧'; 'a surjection ψ : P0 := W⟦x_1, ..., x_d⟧ → A0 … generated by an element of the form p − f')
items.note: Consumer corollary in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay importing the common coefficient map requested at R03.1 by this paper and accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B route 4, together with R03.3 regular-local dimension/depth and complete-intersection inputs. The extra regular-local isomorphism/hypersurface conclusion differs from André’s finite parameter presentation; neither is substituted for the other. The earlier assertion that no layer owns the coefficient construction is removed. Exact Cohen construction remains a missing source addition, not a built node. The paper applies the corollary after enlarging the residue field to an algebraically closed one.
proofSteps: Import the chosen coefficient map iota from cohen-coefficient-ring/R03.1; map W(k)⟦x_1,…,x_d⟧ onto A0 using that same iota and the chosen generators. R03.3 supplies the regular-local dimension and hypersurface arguments for the consumer corollary.
Unramified case: p, x_2, …, x_d is a regular system of parameters, so W(k)⟦x_2,…,x_d⟧→A0 is a surjection of regular local rings of the same dimension, hence an isomorphism.

Ramified case: the kernel is a height-one prime of the factorial ring W(k)⟦x_1,…,x_d⟧, hence principal. A generator lies outside the square of the maximal ideal because A0 is regular, and p ∈ m² makes it a unit multiple of p−f with f ∈ (p,x_1,…,x_d)². p-torsionfreeness and p-adic completeness of A0 give p ∤ f and no constant term.

unitTests.statement: A0 = Z_p[x]/(x²−p) is ramified (p = x² ∈ m², d = 1), and the kernel of Z_p⟦x⟧→A0 is generated by p−x².

unitTests.name: cohen-structure.test_2
unitTests.statement: A0 = Z_p⟦y⟧ is unramified of dimension 2 and equals W(F_p)⟦x_2⟧.

Under a compatible separable residue extension, the parameter-evaluation square commutes. No perfectoid or splitting theorem is a prerequisite of the coefficient input.

uses.how: Import the chosen coefficient map iota from cohen-coefficient-ring/R03.1; map W(k)⟦x_1,…,x_d⟧ onto A0 using that same iota and the chosen generators. R03.3 supplies the regular-local dimension and hypersurface arguments for the consumer corollary.

items.name: Flat local extension with prescribed residue field
items.statement: Let (A0,m,k) be a Noetherian local ring and K/k a field extension. There is a flat local map A0→A0′ of Noetherian local rings such that mA0′ is the maximal ideal of A0′ and A0′/mA0′ ≅ K over k (EGA 0_III, 10.3.1). If A0 is regular, so is A0′, and A0′ may be replaced by its completion.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.2, p. 8 ('We are free to replace A0 by noetherian regular local rings that are faithfully flat over it. Thus, we may assume that A0 is complete … and has an algebraically closed residue field k')
items.note: Added in review. Neither library has it, and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 plans "residue-field extension" only inside its complete local coefficient categories.
proofSteps: Construct it as in EGA 0_III 10.3.1 by transfinite adjunction of monogenic residue extensions along flat local maps. That the colimit is Noetherian is the substantive step and must be proved, not assumed.
Flatness and mA0′ maximal give dim A0′ = dim A0 and equal embedding dimensions, so A0′ is regular when A0 is. Completion preserves regularity and faithful flatness.

unitTests.name: residue-field-extension.test_1
unitTests.statement: For A0 = Z_p and K an algebraic closure of F_p, A0′ = W(K) works: it is flat over Z_p with maximal ideal pW(K).

uses.where: Proof of Proposition 5.2, p. 8 ('We are free to replace A0 by noetherian regular local rings that are faithfully flat over it. Thus, we may assume that A0 is complete … and has an algebraically closed residue field k')
uses.how: Construct it as in EGA 0_III 10.3.1 by transfinite adjunction of monogenic residue extensions along flat local maps. That the colimit is Noetherian is the substantive step and must be proved, not assumed.

items.name: Local and complete reduction for the derived splitting
items.statement: Let A0 be a Noetherian regular ring and f0:X0→Spec(A0) proper and surjective. Let Q be the cone of A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) and α ∈ Hom_{D(A0)}(Q,A0[1]) its connecting map, so that the unit splits iff α = 0. Q is pseudo-coherent, so for every flat A0→A0′ the natural map Hom_{D(A0)}(Q,A0[1])⊗_{A0}A0′→Hom_{D(A0′)}(Q⊗^L_{A0}A0′,A0′[1]) is an isomorphism (Stacks 0A6A), and by flat base change Q⊗^L_{A0}A0′ is the cone of the unit for X0×_{A0}Spec(A0′). Hence α = 0 iff its image vanishes over the completion of the localization at every maximal ideal of A0. These are complete regular local rings of equal characteristic 0, of equal characteristic p, or of mixed characteristic (0,p); the proof of Theorem 6.1 treats the last.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 11 ('We may assume A0 is a regular local ring'), with the passage to the complete mixed-characteristic setting of the proof of Theorem 5.4
items.note: Added in review, with E15: the paper states the reduction without the characteristic split or the reason a derived splitting may be checked locally. The equal-characteristic rings are the cases credited to [Ko] and [Bh1] (equal-characteristic).
proofSteps: RΓ(X0,O_X0) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology (proper-cohomology), so it and the cone Q are pseudo-coherent.

Apply Stacks 0A6A (Lemma 15.101.2, case 3: A0→A0′ flat, Q pseudo-coherent, A0[1] bounded below) and take H^0. Flat base change for the quasi-compact, separated X0 (Stacks 02KH, Lemma 30.5.2) identifies Q⊗^L_{A0}A0′ with the cone for the base change, compatibly with the units.
Hom_{D(A0)}(Q,A0[1]) is a finite A0-module, so an element vanishes iff it vanishes in every localization at a maximal ideal, and each local ring maps faithfully flatly to its completion.

unitTests.name: derived-local-reduction.test_1
unitTests.statement: For A0 = Z the rings produced are the Z_p, all of mixed characteristic, so no equal-characteristic case occurs.

unitTests.name: derived-local-reduction.test_2
unitTests.statement: For A0 = Q[x] every completed local ring at a maximal ideal is a power series ring in one variable over a finite extension of Q, so only the characteristic-0 branch is used.

uses.where: Proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 11 ('We may assume A0 is a regular local ring'), with the passage to the complete mixed-characteristic setting of the proof of Theorem 5.4
uses.how: RΓ(X0,O_X0) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology (proper-cohomology), so it and the cone Q are pseudo-coherent.

items.name: Detection of a perfect-cone obstruction modulo p^m and after the perfectoid extensions
items.statement: Let A0 be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), Q0 a perfect complex of A0-modules and α0 ∈ Hom_{D(A0)}(Q0,A0[1]); put P = RHom_{A0}(Q0,A0). The towers {Hom_{D(A0)}(Q0,A0/p^m[1])}_m and {H^1(P)/p^m}_m are pro-isomorphic, because the tower {H^2(P)[p^m]}_m, whose transition maps are multiplication by p, is pro-zero. Hence if α0 ≠ 0, then α0/p^m ≠ 0 for some m ≥ 3, by Krull's intersection theorem for the finite module H^1(P). For g ∈ A0 coprime to p and A0→A∞,0→A∞ as in Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 2.3, the map Hom_{D(A0)}(Q0,A0/p^m[1])⊗_{A0}A∞→Hom_{D(A∞)}(Q0⊗^L_{A0}A∞,A∞/p^m[1]) is an almost isomorphism for p^(1/p^∞), and the annihilator argument of the proof of Theorem 5.4 gives k with (pg)^(1/p^k) ∉ Ann(α∞/p^m).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 11 ('Repeating the argument in the proof of Theorem 5.4'); the perfect-complex form of Lemma 5.3 and of the first half of the proof of Theorem 5.4, p. 10
items.note: Added in review; the extraction left this step as a G5 obligation inside derived-summand. For a finite extension of a regular local ring, B0/A0 is itself perfect, so one statement can serve Theorems 5.4 and 6.1. The Krull argument here does not use completeness of A0 (compare E14).
proofSteps: Q0 is perfect, so RHom_{A0}(Q0,A0/p^m) = P⊗^L_{A0}A0/p^m, and its H^1 sits in 0→H^1(P)/p^m→Hom_{D(A0)}(Q0,A0/p^m[1])→H^2(P)[p^m]→0. The finite module H^2(P) has bounded p-power torsion, killed by some p^M, so the cokernel tower is pro-zero.
H^1(P) is finite, so Krull's intersection theorem gives m with α0 ∉ p^mH^1(P); enlarge m to at least 3.

RHom commutes with derived base change along A0→A∞ for perfect Q0 (Stacks 0A6A, case 1). The almost flatness of A0/p^m→A∞,0/p^m→A∞/p^m makes the comparison of H^1 an almost isomorphism, and the annihilator calculation of obstruction-detection applies verbatim.

unitTests.name: perfect-cone-detection.test_1
unitTests.statement: For A0 = Z_(p) and Q0 = Z_(p)/p, P = RHom(Q0,A0) has H^1(P) = Z/p and H^2(P) = 0, and Hom(Q0,A0/p^m[1]) = Ext^1(Z/p,Z/p^m) = Z/p for every m ≥ 1.

uses.where: Proof of Theorem 6.1, p. 11 ('Repeating the argument in the proof of Theorem 5.4'); the perfect-complex form of Lemma 5.3 and of the first half of the proof of Theorem 5.4, p. 10
uses.how: Q0 is perfect, so RHom_{A0}(Q0,A0/p^m) = P⊗^L_{A0}A0/p^m, and its H^1 sits in 0→H^1(P)/p^m→Hom_{D(A0)}(Q0,A0/p^m[1])→H^2(P)[p^m]→0. The finite module H^2(P) has bounded p-power torsion, killed by some p^M, so the cokernel tower is pro-zero.

items.name: Almost vanishing of a perfect-cone obstruction from the annuli
items.statement: In the setting of perfect-cone-detection, put Q∞ = Q0⊗^L_{A0}A∞ and K = RHom_{A∞}(Q∞,A∞/p^m). If for every n ≥ 1 the image of α∞/p^m in Hom_{D(A∞)}(Q∞,A∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m[1]) is almost zero for p^(1/p^∞), then α∞/p^m is almost zero for (pg)^(1/p^∞). routes.title: Direct summands and big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
routes.brief: Coalesce with DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay, the new roadmap proposed by PAPER-ANDRE-18-B and accepted by its review (design DESIGN-DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay); this route replaces the earlier proposal of a Part II of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, which would have opened a second roadmap in the same direction. State the direct summand theorem once, with André's and Bhatt's proofs as alternative routes, and add the derived direct summand theorem. Build on Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra), importing its complete local coefficient and regular local homological algebra rather than recreating those foundations. The first final theorem is: every finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular admits an A0-linear retraction. The second is: for every proper surjective f0:X0→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular, the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) splits in D(A0). Neither retraction is required to be multiplicative. Import Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) P0–P3; Perfectoid quotients and their prismatic prerequisites (PerfectoidQuotients) Q0:integral-algebra and Q3; the quantitative tower theorem of the shared Part II Perfectoid rings and spaces, Part II: ramification and Riemann extension (PerfectoidRamification); Derived de Rham cohomology and its algebraic foundations (DerivedDeRhamCohomology) DD.1; Enhanced derived categories of sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves) E1 and E2; the modification theory of Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.4; the integral generic-fibre map of Foundations of adic spaces, Part II (AdicSpacesPartII) R2; the regular-local homological algebra of Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) R03.1, R03.3 and P7; and, from the Tau Ceti roadmap Stable reduction of curves and stable maps (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction), layer 2's coherent proper pushforward and layer 4's blowups, which are imported, never re-planned. Construct the unramified and ramified regular local perfectoid covers separately, prove both positive Tor almost vanishing and detection of ordinary modules, and track the (!!) and star normalization steps. Import R03.1’s chosen Cohen coefficient map and its compatible coefficient changes, shared with accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B route 4. Prove only the extra regular-local isomorphism/hypersurface corollary (cohen-structure) using that map and R03.3’s dimension/depth inputs; do not rebuild the coefficient ring. Prove the localization/completion, component, residue-field and discriminant reductions (residue-field-extension), completing before the domain reduction (E14, E9), obstruction detection modulo p^m and its p²g-to-pg annihilator calculation, and almost vanishing on every annulus with its lim-one removal. For the derived theorem prove the perfectness of proper coherent cohomology, the local and complete reduction of the derived obstruction (derived-local-reduction, E15), the perfect-cone obstruction calculus (perfect-cone-detection, perfect-cone-limit), generic multisection reduction and corrected Proposition 6.2 with generic finite-étale SURJECTIVITY in mixed characteristic. Do not replace coherent base change by étale proper base change or ordinary base change without Tor control. Read the original equal-characteristic inputs and GR2 non-Noetherian domination theorem before closing the graph. Coordinate ownership of any splinter predicate with PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23's accepted route 10, a Part II of SchemeAndStackFoundations whose item splinter defines the predicate; these statements can use explicit retractions and need no duplicate singularity vocabulary. Remark 5.5 is a question in this source, not a proved acceptance target; G8 records its later answer. Remark 1.3 frames the two proofs: André proved Theorem 1.1 first, and Bhatt replaces the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma by the quantitative Riemann extension theorem (Theorem 4.2), keeping André's flatness lemma (Theorem 2.3) as the essential new ingredient. Continuation: proper H^0 integrality/localization/affinization are pinned library imports. Use the named SF.4 Stacks 0815–081T modification items and their R2 integral chart adapter. The bridge from ordinary proper base change needs only the E1 unit-compatible comparison morphism and composition of retractions, not its being an isomorphism. Also: prove the reduction to a finite domain extension explicitly (source issue E9) and state Theorem 5.4 with its finite extension (E10).
